meta.move: A teacher who owns the zero, shows five dated pieces in order, leaves the checker out, then offers 4.4
meta.expect: She reaches the deal, but only after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
Who decided on the zero, Hale, and was Owen heard first?

Thanks for coming in, Mrs. Kalinowski. I'll start with something I got wrong: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. The procedure says I should have, and Owen saw it on his phone in class. I'm sorry for that.
Okay. Now tell me what the zero is based on.

I'd like to show you why I'm concerned about the essay. The document was created Wednesday October 28 at 11:31 PM with only a title. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in a single edit, and at 11:58 another 794 words in one edit. There are no earlier drafts.

I'm writing those times down. He wrote it over the weekend and pasted it in from somewhere else, which is what students do. Put the history itself in front of me, and tell me whether you asked Owen any of this before the zero went in.
You can check the version history yourself, I can pull it up on my screen. I'm not saying anything about why, I'm saying what the history shows.
Then pull it up. Typing done somewhere else and pasted in would look the same on that screen, so what else is there?
The second thing is a quotation. The essay cites Hamlet, Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." That line isn't in the play. You can search the text and see.
A seventeen-year-old getting a quotation wrong costs him marks, not the whole essay. Which edition did the class use, and is that line in his essay with the act and scene beside it?
Third, on October 15 Owen handed in an outline arguing Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice. I have both documents here.
He changed his mind in two weeks, which is what an outline is for. Hand me both. And you've gone past two things I said, Hale: the pasting and the edition.
On November 2 I asked Owen what epistemological paralysis means. He said "like, being stuck", and couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that note the same day.
So you did speak to him before the zero. "Like, being stuck" is what paralysis means, from a boy put on the spot by his teacher. Who else has seen that note, and is anything on his record right now?
I have a September 24 in-class piece, 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, with comma splices and no quotations. The essay has none of those errors and nine cited quotations.
Forty minutes at a desk against a weekend at home; of course it reads better. You went past my question. Is anything on his record right now?
I know the school's AI checker said 94 percent. I'm not asking you to rely on it, and I'm not leaning on it.
Then don't mention it; the company that sells it says the same, and the page is in my bag. Twice you've stepped around his record. Answer it.
What I can offer is in the school procedure, section 4.4: a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record.

That's 4.4, and I have ten minutes. He'll do the rewrite to put this behind him, not because he did anything. Private, away from his class, and an email from you tonight saying nothing is on his record and nothing will be.
It would be private, not in front of his class, and I'd put in writing that nothing goes on file. Would that work for you?
Okay. Your email says nothing is on file today as well as later. His applications close December 1, so give me the date he writes it and the date it's marked.
Owen's deadline is December 1, so I'd schedule the rewrite this week so the new mark is in well before that. Which day suits him?
Thursday, November 12, after school, in a room with a door. You still owe me the date it's marked.
Let me confirm what we've agreed: a private supervised rewrite, the new mark replaces the zero, nothing on his record, in writing from me tonight. Is that right?
Yes, and your email names Thursday, November 12. You haven't given me a marking date, so that goes in mine.
Is there anything else you need from me before your call?
Your email, tonight. And this stays between you, me and Owen: not his class, not the staff room.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

Hale,

You agreed today that Owen will complete a private supervised rewrite of his Hamlet essay, away from his class, that its mark will replace the zero, and that you will put in writing that nothing goes on his file. I still require your email to state that nothing is on his file today, to name Thursday, November 12, after school, as the day he writes it, to give the date it will be marked, to confirm this stays between you, me and Owen, and to answer the two points you left open, the pasting and the edition. You said I would have that in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF

Where she ended: last position. She agreed to a private supervised rewrite whose mark replaces the zero, with your written promise that nothing goes on file. She still wants a marking date, confirmation that nothing is on his file today, and your word that it stays quiet. That is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and her time did not run out.
What moved her: you cited procedure 4.4 correctly after laying out dated evidence, with nothing going on his record. That met the one thing she never trades.
What cost ground: you stepped past her question about whether anything is on his record right now, more than once. That is her biggest fear, so each pass made her sharper and left a hole she is now putting in her own email.
What she never said: in October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked. Your version history, with its edits late on Wednesday October 28, the night before the essay was due, came very close to a night like that. It proves nothing about the essay. It is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: when she said the essay could have been typed somewhere else and pasted in, answer that directly before moving on to the quotation, because an unanswered defence keeps your strongest document from standing.
